item.title: CoMLRL Quick Start
item.description:
This tutorial demonstrates a simple two-agent training task with a length-ratio reward. Both agents receive the same prompt and generate independently; the second agent does not see the first agent’s response. The reward encourages the second output to contain 2–3× as many characters as the first. It does not evaluate story quality or semantic collaboration.

Users can run the example from an installed source checkout:

python examples/story-len-ratio.py

Memory requirements depend on the model, number of agents, batch size, and response length. W&B logging is disabled by default. The --wandb flag enables it; --wandb-project and --wandb-entity are optional.

item.title: Installation
item.description:
CoMLRL can be installed from PyPI, conda-forge, or source. Python 3.10 or later is largely recommended. Users can install a PyTorch build compatible with their device.

Installation from PyPI#

pip install comlrl
# Install PyTorch compatible with your device.

Installation from conda-forge#

conda install -c conda-forge comlrl
# Install PyTorch compatible with your device.

item.title: Multi-Agent REINFORCE
item.description:
REINFORCE is a class of policy-gradient methods that optimize the policy directly using sampled returns. These methods are widely used for LLM fine-tuning because of their simplicity and efficiency. Examples include GRPO, Dr. GRPO, RLOO, ReMax, TreeRPO, and REINFORCE++. REINFORCE can be extended to multi-agent settings, where multiple LLM agents respond at each turn and their joint responses receive a shared reward.

item.title: Multi-Turn Algorithm
item.description:
Many complex problems require more than one turn to solve. LLM agents interact with the environment to obtain useful feedback from other models or tools in the system.

Multi-Turn MAGRPO#

Multi-turn MAGRPO builds a rollout tree whose branches represent different joint responses (TreeRPO).

Each episode begins with a task sampled from the dataset, which provides the initial observations \( \mathbf{o}_0=\{o_{1, 0}, \cdots, o_{n, 0}\} \) and histories \( \mathbf{h}_0=\{h_{1, 0}, \cdots, h_{n, 0}\} \) for all agents. At each turn, agents generate a group of joint responses \( \mathbf{a}^{\mathcal{G}}_t\gets\boldsymbol{\pi}^{\mathcal{G}}(\cdot|\mathbf{h}_t) \) from their current observation-action history \( \mathbf{h}_t \). Each response starts a distinct rollout. Agents receive joint rewards \( r^{(g)}_{t} \) for each response, based on the accumulated history and current joint action \( \mathbf{a}^{(g)}_{t} \in \mathbf{a}^{\mathcal{G}}_{t} \). Each rollout then evolves independently, producing new joint observations \( \mathbf{o}^{\mathcal{G}}_{t+1} \) as the environment evolves and branching into further rollouts at the next turn \( t+1 \). This process continues until the terminal turn \( H \).

item.title: Support
item.description:
Support#

We are happy to help with issues encountered while using CoMLRL.

Report Issues#

The following steps can help users resolve or report an issue:

  1. Users can first consult the documentation, including the search feature (Ctrl + K).

  2. A search of existing GitHub Issues may reveal reports of the same problem.

  3. A minimal reproducible example helps diagnose the issue. A few lines of code that demonstrate the problem can lead to a faster response.

item.title: Training Framework
item.description:
MARLHF and MADPO share a training framework. Actors generate joint responses, and the task reward ranks them to form preference pairs. The iterative trainers repeat this process against a comparator, while a replay buffer selects the pairs for each update. MARLHF and MADPO describe the two learning objectives.

Collaboration Modes#

collaboration_mode sets the trainable actor layout, and comparator_generation_mode sets the comparator layout in iterative training.

Actor layout Comparator layout Joint responses
Decentralized Decentralized Each role generates its own response on both sides of the comparison.
Decentralized Centralized Separate actors are compared with one comparator that generates all roles’ responses.
Centralized Centralized One actor and one comparator each generate a complete joint response.

The diagram compares the three supported layouts, with the actor on the left and the comparator \( \varpi \) on the right.

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
Contributing#

Contributions to CoMLRL are welcome. This guide covers issue reporting, code changes, and codebase maintenance.

Development Guidelines#

  1. Contributors can fork the upstream repository.
  2. The following commands clone the fork and synchronize it with upstream: 
     git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/CoMLRL.git
 cd CoMLRL
 git remote add upstream https://github.com/OpenMLRL/CoMLRL.git
 git fetch upstream
 git checkout -b feature/<short-description> upstream/main
 git fetch upstream && git rebase upstream/main
  3. Contributors can implement new features or fix bugs and update the documentation as needed.
  4. Changes can be submitted to the upstream repository as a pull request for review.

item.title: Model Loading & Saving
item.description:
CoMLRL supports both homogeneous and heterogeneous models from Hugging Face or local directories. Users can specify Hugging Face model identifiers through agent_model/critic_model for homogeneous setups, or provide agents/critics lists for heterogeneous setups. Trained agents can be saved and loaded into a new trainer for further training.

Loading LLM Agents#

Homogeneous Agents#

Users can initialize homogeneous agents by setting agent_model to a single model identifier and leaving agents=None. For trainers with a separate num_agents constructor argument, users can set it alongside the matching configuration value; the configuration alone does not override it.

item.title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic
item.description:
Actor-Critic (AC) methods are widely used policy gradient methods that use critics to support training. AC methods can achieve lower variance and better sample efficiency than REINFORCE, but this requires careful design and tuning of the critic to ensure stable training. In Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), Actor-Critic methods include Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (MAAC) and Independent Actor-Critic (IAC).

MAAC#

Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (MAAC) uses one Centralized Critic (CC) across agents to evaluate joint histories with critic_type="v", or joint history-action pairs with critic_type="q". The critic receives the agents’ prompts joined into a single text sequence; Q mode also includes their generated completions.

item.title: Multi-Agent RLHF
item.description:
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (MARLHF) fits a joint reward model to preference pairs, then trains the policies with RL using the learned reward. CoMLRL generates the preference labels with the task reward_func.

The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → Stage 1: joint reward learning → Stage 2: policy reinforcement learning. Because the reward model scores the team’s complete response, separate actors learn from one shared reward. MADPO instead optimizes the policies directly from the pairs, without a reward model.

Changelog#

Version 1.4.2#

  • Support more comparator models (commit e1b3d80).
  • Fix the homogeneous generation issue (commit 11d89a9).

Version 1.4.1#

  • Support using the comparator as a centralized coordinator (PR #69).
  • Allow deploying LLM agents, the reward model, and the comparator on different devices (commit 7cbb792).
  • Allow copying current models as comparators on new devices (commit d8d493a).
  • Optimize GPU memory usage by promptly releasing unused models (commit d0c6376).

Version 1.4.0#

  • Add online preference-learning methods (PR #68).
  • Add dataset drift logger.

Version 1.3.9#

  • Add offline preference-learning methods such as MADPO and MARLHF (PR #67).

Version 1.3.8#

  • Allow using a reference model for all algorithms (PR #65).
  • Unify the logger between different trainers (PR #66).

Version 1.3.7#

  • Remove the redundant sampling hyperparameters in algorithms.
  • Allow multi-GPU training with MP (see results in PR #62).

Version 1.3.6#

  • Fix a critical bug in loading heterogeneous models and refactor the model-loading logic (see results in PR #60).
  • Polish the docs.

Version 1.3.5#

  • Add unit tests for hyperparameter constraints.
  • Clean legacy interfaces.

Version 1.3.4#

  • Fix the bug in loading heterogeneous models and refactor the loading logic.
  • Enable MBGD in MAGRPO to align with MAAC and IAC.
  • Remove redundant and legacy hyperparameters (e.g., model kwargs, patching hyperparameters).
  • Clean up multi-device legacy code, such as drop last and num_workers.
  • Add unit tests for model loading and separate them from CI as a badge.
  • Clean short functions.
  • Reorganize the docs and align the parameters.

Version 1.3.3#

  • Compact the MAREINFORCETrainer derivation and move it to the new folder.
  • Unify the interface for different trainers.
  • Remove redundant patches and wrappers.
  • Reorganize the variables in the config YAML files.

Version 1.3.2#

  • Fix wandb logging issue in MAGRPOTrainer.

Version 1.3.1#

  • Allow batch training in MAGRPOTrainer, IACTrainer, and MAACTrainer.
  • Allow multi-turn training in IACTrainer and MAACTrainer.
  • Change the x-axis from data_step to env_step.

Version 1.3.0#

  • Use TD error as the critic update target in IACTrainer and MAACTrainer.

Version 1.2.9#

  • Add MAACTrainer (separate centralized critic); both IACTrainer and MAACTrainer now support single-turn training.

Version 1.2.8#

  • The critic in IACTrainer now estimates V rather than Q.

Version 1.2.7#

  • Change IPPOTrainer to IACTrainer.

Version 1.2.6#

  • Include MAGRPO, MAREINFORCE, MARLOO, MAREMAX, and IPPO trainers for multi-agent reinforcement learning with LLMs.
  • Support for multi-turn training with custom external feedback mechanisms.
  • LLM collaboration environments for various tasks.
  • Comprehensive documentation and examples for getting started.

item.title: Dataset Loading
item.description:
Users can keep task inputs and metadata in the same dataset, with a separate split for evaluation. This guide prepares training and evaluation data for the length-ratio task from the quick start.

Dataset Splits#

Each dataset row is a dictionary. The default formatter reads its prompt field; additional fields can hold targets, labels, test cases, or other information required by the reward function. Trainers pass the original row to the reward function through batch_items.

item.title: Multi-Agent DPO
item.description:
Multi-Agent Direct Preference Optimization (MADPO) trains the agents directly from preferred and rejected joint responses, without a reward model or a separate RL stage. Its loss combines all agents’ preference margins, so each policy learns from the team’s outcome.

The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → joint preference loss → policy updates. MARLHF uses the same pairs to fit a joint reward model first and then trains the policies with RL.

item.title: Logging Metric
item.description:
CoMLRL supports local evaluation records, training curves in Weights & Biases, and task-specific metrics. The examples use the trainer and held-out split from Dataset Loading.

Local Metrics#

Evaluation returns a metrics dictionary even when W&B is disabled. Users can save this dictionary locally to record a completed evaluation:

import json
from pathlib import Path

# Use the MAGRPO trainer and eval_dataset from the Dataset Loading guide.
metrics = trainer.evaluate(num_eval_samples=len(eval_dataset))
Path("eval-metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(metrics, indent=2) + "\n")

item.title: Training Parallelization
item.description:
CoMLRL trainers run in a Python process. For IAC, parallel_training="none" is the default; "mp" enables scheduling agents and critics on explicitly assigned devices. Neither mode requires a job scheduler.

Model Parallelization#

Users can configure IACTrainer by passing an IACConfig through its args parameter. The following configuration uses four visible CUDA devices and two agents:

from comlrl.trainers.actor_critic import IACConfig

config = IACConfig(
 num_agents=2,
 num_turns=1,
 use_separate_critic=True,
 parallel_training="mp",
 agent_devices=["cuda:0", "cuda:1"],
 critic_devices=["cuda:2", "cuda:3"],
)

agent_devices is required in "mp" mode. critic_devices is also required when use_separate_critic=True. Each model stays on its assigned device; this does not split an individual model across GPUs. Responses are passed to the reward function, and the rewards are used for each agent’s update.

item.title: Q&A
item.description:
What are the differences between CoMLRL and other multi-LLM training frameworks?

Many approaches train role-conditioned agents with shared parameters using single-agent RL frameworks. Distinct agents better represent heterogeneous LLMs with different capabilities and more directly reflect the multi-agent setting.

CoMLRL supports separate actors with decentralized execution, including training with a centralized critic. Its centralized collaboration mode instead uses one actor to generate the complete joint response. The available trainers include REINFORCE, Actor-Critic, and Multi-Agent Preference Learning; each method’s page describes its implemented objective and constraints.
